[[File:Asen A. Hadjiolov.png|thumb|180px|Asen A. Hadjiolov]]
'''Asen A. Hadjiolov''' ({{langx|bg|Асен А. Хаджиолов}}) (December 10, 1930{{snd}}April 22, 1996) was one of the most distinguished scientists in [[Bulgaria]], and was a member of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite book |chapter=HADJIOLOV, Asen A. |title= The International Who's Who 1992-1993 |edition=56th  |page= [https://archive.org/details/internationalwho1992lond/page/648/mode/2up?view=theater 648] |publisher= Europa Publications Limited |place= London |year= 1992 |url=https://archive.org/details/internationalwho1992lond/page/n5/mode/2up?view=theater |isbn = 0-946653-84-4 |accessdate= 23 January 2026 |via= [[Internet Archive]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author = Hadjiolova, K.V., Bachellerie, JP., Vaptzarova, K., George Markov, Panteley Popov, Kalcho Markov & George Russev |title= Asen Hadjiolov, remembered |journal = Chromosoma |date= June 1997 |issue = 105 |pages= 388–390 |doi= 10.1007/BF02510474}}</ref>

==Vita in brief==
[[Image:RRNA.jpg|thumb|150px|left|The algorithm for life<ref>Paul Schimmel and Rebecca Alexander Science (1998) Vol. 281. no. 5377, pp. 658 - 659</ref> - Three-dimensional structure of ''[[Escherichia coli|E. coli]]''<ref>Barbara S. Schuwirth et al., Science (2005) Vol. 310. no. 5749, pp. 827 - 834</ref> [[ribosomal RNA]],<ref>Anders Liljas in Science (1999) Vol. 285. no. 5436, pp. 2077 - 2078</ref> showing extensive base-pairing between different regions of single stranded RNA<ref>Nenad Ban et al., Science (2000) Vol. 289. no. 5481, pp. 905 - 920</ref>]]

[[Image:BAS-IMM50 percent.jpg|thumb|100px|right|Former Institute of Cell Biology & Morphology]]

Hadjiolov's scholarly research on the [[nucleolus]] and [[ribosome]] biogenesis and his leadership in the scientific community touched many lives. As a young researcher he followed the path of his father: Professor Asen I. Hadjiolov was a well-known [[Bulgarians|Bulgarian]] [[histologist]] and [[cytologist]]. Hadjiolov began experimental work in the Department of [[Biochemistry]] of the Medical Faculty of [[Sofia]] and was awarded the PhD in 1958 for his studies on the role of [[nucleic acids]] in [[cancer]]. In 1963 Hadjiolov became chair of the Department of Molecular [[Genetics]] in the Central Laboratory of [[Biochemistry]], which was transformed into the Institute of [[Molecular Biology]] of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1969. During his early years, Hadjiolov had the chance to work with such eminent scientists as F.B. Straub ([[Budapest]]), R Grabar (Paris), the [[Nobel Prize]] winner [[Fritz Lipmann]]<ref>[https://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/medicine/laureates/1953/lipmann-bio.html Fritz Lipmann Biography - The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1953]</ref> ([[Cold Spring Harbor, New York]]) and later with R. Cox (London)<ref>Hadjiolov AA, Cox RA. Biochem J. (1973) 135(2):349-51</ref><ref>Hadjiolov AA et al., Biochem J. (1975) 147(3):625-8.</ref> and D. Sabatini (New York). Early on, he became fascinated by the structure and biosynthesis of [[ribosomal RNA]] (rRNA) and the biogenesis of [[eukaryotic]] [[ribosomes]].

==Mechanisms of regulation of rRNA synthesis==
[[Image:HdjiolovOlegLab.jpg|thumb|100px|right|One of Hadjiolov's lab where rRNA was sequenced]]
Hadjiolov's laboratory was the first to provide reliable evidence that the change in the rate of rRNA synthesis in higher [[eukaryotes]] is not accompanied by alterations in the number of active [[genes]].<ref>Hadjiolov and Nikolaev (1976) Prog Biophys Mol Biol. 1976;31(2):95-144</ref> During his active research years Hadjiolov published more than hundred of articles focused on the [[ribosome]] (see [[PubMed]] for a complete list). Hadjiolov's list of publications totals 106 listed in PubMed. Hadjiolov's contribution to the world's science can also be measured by contribution of the scientists he recruited and supported throughout his career. All together the heritage of his group exceeds 1,000 articles annotated by [[PubMed]], which matches today's highest quantitative achievements in science. For example, the most cited author since 1994 by the [[Institute for Scientific Information]]'s Citation Report, Dr. John C. Reed ([[Burnham Institute for Medical Research]]) and his group have reached similar number of articles ([[PubMed]]:728 as of April 4, 2007).<ref>[http://www.sciencewatch.com/may-june2000/sw_may-june2000_page4.htm Science Watch 2000] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070428074213/http://www.sciencewatch.com/may-june2000/sw_may-june2000_page4.htm |date=April 28, 2007 }}</ref>
